title: A complete 6HB origami: periodic ends, linear polymers and circles

sections.title: Create a standard honeycomb 6HB
sections.body: Build the six-helix ring on a honeycomb lattice. Use your own descriptive filenames; the __e2e__ names shown here identify the isolated guide capture. This lesson uses a 1,236 bp initial extrusion; Seamed Autoscaffold adjusts the terminal turns to produce a single 7,560-nt scaffold matching p7560. Full representation is used for construction; later images explicitly demonstrate visualization choices.

sections.title: Route scaffold and staples
sections.body: Run Seamed Autoscaffold to obtain matched end faces, then Standard Full Autostaple to route the interior staples. Autoscaffold can extend individual helix ends; inspect the routed scaffold length rather than assuming it equals six times the initial extrusion length.

sections.title: Make the ends periodic
sections.body: Route for Polymerization fills the bare terminal scaffold regions with connector staples and joins their terminal tips across the periodic seam. Each copy retains its own scaffold. The bridging staples join adjacent repeats; in the part they are recorded as periodic seam strands.

sections.title: Assign the scaffold and staple sequences
sections.body: Assign p7560 after routing so the entire 7,560-nt scaffold receives the intended sequence. Full Autostaple initially uses M13mp18; this explicit assignment replaces it. Then assign complementary staple sequences, including the periodic bridges. The saved example is checked for undefined bases.

sections.title: Inspect topology and sequences in the cadnano editor
sections.body: Open Origami Editor to inspect the same saved part as a flat strand diagram. Check scaffold continuity, staple crossovers, terminal connector staples and sequence assignment. The path view preserves base-pair indices even when the 3D part is bent.

sections.title: Use the periodic boundary view
sections.body: Enable PBC to display translucent copies of the terminal regions beside the opposite ends. The two red boundary sliders define the display period P = far − near. Dashed seam connections pass through that boundary. Dragging a boundary changes this inspection view; editing a mirrored strand changes the real part. The view resets when disabled or reloaded.

sections.title: Choose useful 3D visualizations
sections.body: Full shows nucleotide geometry; Cylinders simplify the bundle shape. Length coloring helps inspect the staple length distribution. The temperature overlay cycles through domain melting temperature and total staple folding temperature; these estimates support inspection rather than proving assembly yield. Periodic Seam Connections reveals the normally hidden long seam arcs in the single-part view.

sections.title: Create an actual linear polymer assembly
sections.body: Create a separate assembly and add the saved periodic part. The “via periodic boundary” option derives repeat placement from its seam strands. Chain length is the total number of units including the seed. Forward, Backward and Both choose where new repeats are placed relative to it.

sections.title: Bend a repeat for a circular polymer
sections.body: Open the straight part and use Save As to create a separate circular unit. Tools → Bend offers Curve to make polymer circle after periodic strands exist. Set six units; the tool derives the curvature from the periodic seam span. Direction rotates the bending plane. This chapter demonstrates CAD curvature and geometric ring placement; it does not apply loop/skip compensation or validate the relaxed physical shape. The repeat is still a part; copies are created later in its assembly.

sections.title: Build and inspect the circular assembly
sections.body: Create a new assembly using the bent unit and choose six total repeats. Verify both the rotational and translational residuals before polymerizing. A circular arrangement requires the accumulated repeat transform to return to the starting frame; the closure check measures that alignment. Consecutive seam mates remain explicit assembly operations.

steps.caption: For this staggered 6HB, the physical repeat is 1260 bp while the default bounding span is 1267 bp. Move the far boundary 7 bp inward: the “overlap 7 bp” display lets the staggered ends interlock. This changes only the inspection period; assembly placement comes from the recorded seams.

steps.caption: For this exact 6HB, the automatic estimate leaves a 0.515 nm six-unit closure residual. Uncheck Curve to make polymer circle and refine Angle to 60.3229°, keeping Direction 0° and planes −12–1254 bp. The recorded manual setting meets the 0.5 nm closure tolerance; this value is specific to this example.
